In [[mathematics]], '''Grothendieck's connectedness theorem''',<ref name="auto">{{harvnb|Grothendieck|Raynaud|2005|loc=XIII.2.1}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Lazarsfeld|2004|loc=theorem 3.3.16}}</ref> states that if ''A'' is a complete [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]] [[local ring]] whose spectrum is ''k''-connected and ''f'' is in the [[maximal ideal]], then Spec(''A''/''fA'') is (''k''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)-connected. Here a [[Noetherian scheme]] is called ''k''-connected if its dimension is greater than ''k'' and the complement of every [[closed set|closed subset]] of dimension less than ''k'' is connected.<ref name="auto"/>

It is a local analogue of [[Bertini's theorem]].
